A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLoRA system and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original hyperparameter sweeps, downstream accuracy measurements, GPU profiling, throughput benchmarks, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original accuracy, makespan, throughput, profiling, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: The shared frozen model, independent adapters, packed forward/backward kernels, DTM algorithm, and job planner remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of heterogeneous training workflows do not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MRPC, CoLA, and WNLI with the same represented task coverage. v2 discusses additional domains and objectives as applications but provides no corresponding new evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Min GPU, Max GPU, Sequential PLoRA, sequential kernel execution, base models, Unsloth default configurations, and single-adapter QLoRA. Newly discussed mLoRA, DoRA, and AdaLoRA are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The 120-configuration search, hyperparameter ranges, zero-shot evaluation, sequence length of 1024, GPU testbeds, tensor-parallel allocations, and benchmark settings are retained. The revised FSDP/pipeline-parallel discussion does not establish new experimental protocols.

E4.justification: v2 omits v1 Sections 3.1–3.2’s additional A10 occupancy observation and quantitative memory-feasibility example comparing one versus two packed adapters. Hyperparameter sensitivity, configuration-transfer analyses, kernel scaling, and the planner/kernel ablation remain, partly relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Variation across hyperparameter configurations is not newly introduced statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 3’s GSM8K improvement of 8.0 percentage points becomes 9.0 in v2 Table 6, correcting the difference between unchanged accuracies of 70.8% and 79.8%. v2 also reports planner overhead below 2.5% and omits the small memory-profiling example. Principal accuracy, makespan, throughput, and kernel results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The scheduling formulations, memory constraints, approximation bound, and proof are retained. Theorem 6.1 becomes Theorem D.1; the FSDP and pipeline-parallel memory formulas already appeared in v1 Appendix A. Relocation and condensed explanations do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The title, introduction, contributions, and conclusion redefine the central scope from accelerating LoRA hyperparameter searches to concurrent training of heterogeneous adapters across tasks, domains, and objectives. The headline speedup claims remain. v2 also removes the contribution-bullet claim of scaling beyond 32 adapters, retaining the supported up-to-32 wording.

C2.justification: v2 adds applicability claims for DoRA and AdaLoRA. It replaces v1’s future-work qualification for FSDP/pipeline parallelism with a statement that the appendix explains deployment, although the memory formulas are retained. Most interpretations of packing, kernel efficiency, and quantization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly describes adapter-specific optimizer states, training data, and loss functions. It drops the Nsight Compute identification and the stated 286 solver calls per DTM invocation. Hardware specifications, implementation stack, CUTLASS tuning parameters, and memory-accounting details otherwise remain available.

R1.justification: v2 removes the dedicated hyperparameter-optimization discussion and its first-work positioning, replacing it with broader concurrent-training positioning and an explicit contrast with mLoRA. It adds discussion and citations concerning LoRA Without Regret, DoRA, AdaLoRA, and LoRA versus full fine-tuning.

P1.justification: The introduction, motivation, contribution list, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. System design is consolidated, while kernel details, the full optimization formulation, theorem, sensitivity study, and supplementary benchmarks are reorganized into appendices. Acknowledgment and impact-statement sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a conference layout with revised title/author formatting, headers, captions, and algorithm presentation. Several tables and the A10 throughput figure move from the main text to appendices, substantially redistributing displays. The seven figures and eight tables are retained rather than replaced by new experimental displays.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves consistency by correcting the GSM8K arithmetic and removing the beyond-32-adapters overstatement, while adding relevant training-system positioning through mLoRA. The principal evidence remains available in the appendices. Gains are limited by broader applicability claims without additional validation, omitted profiling detail, and new unresolved 'name’s' placeholders in Figure 6 and related work.
